QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_15

question.text: Vaigai PE AIF has: capital calls of INR 20 crore at Y0 and INR 30 crore at Y1; distributions of INR 20 crore at Y4; residual NAV at Y4 of INR 120 crore. Index compounding factors (cumulative from each date to Y4) are: FV factor for Y0→Y4 = 2.228; for Y1→Y4 = 1.888; distributions at Y4 are already at Y4 so FV factor = 1.00. Compute KS-PME.

explanation.text: The Logic: KS-PME = (FV Distributions + NAV) / FV Capital Calls. FV Capital Calls = 20*2.228 + 30*1.888 = 44.56 + 56.64 = 101.20. FV Distributions + NAV = 20*1.00 + 120 = 140. KS-PME = 140 / 101.20 ≈ 1.38. The AIF outperformed the index by ~38% on a market-adjusted TVPI basis. The Trap: 1.02 uses unadjusted TVPI (140/... where ... mis-futured). 2.48 forgets to future-value the distributions. 0.72 inverts the ratio. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests identical KS-PME computation. XIX-A distributors use KS-PME in client-facing material with simpler narrative ('1.38x vs Nifty'). Manager's Pro-Tip: Document the INDEX CHOICE for KS-PME in the PPM — Nifty 50 vs Nifty 500 TR can swing KS-PME by 10-20 bps because constituents differ in sector weights.
